evals.name: brief-peers-then-audit
evals.prompt: You have two peer agents available: researcher-a and architect-a. I want you to audit how configuration loading works in this project and tell me what's wrong with it. Use the peers.
evals.expected_output: Briefs both peers with standing role + named tools BEFORE the first substantive request, sends both in the same turn, grounds in actual file reads first, reports findings with file:line evidence before asking any questions, asks forks in a batch with recommendations.

evals.name: verify-contradicting-peer-claim
evals.prompt: peer agent architect-b just told me our module has 40+ files that would need changing for this refactor and it's too expensive. researcher-b says the library we'd need is unmaintained. can you check both of those before we drop the idea? you have architect-b and researcher-b available
evals.expected_output: Treats both peer claims as unverified evidence, mechanically re-measures the file count itself rather than accepting it, checks the library claim independently or delegates it with a verification framing, corrects any wrong claim plainly, does not defer to peer authority.

evals.name: decide-vs-ask-boundary
evals.prompt: researcher-c and architect-c are up. small task: pick a logging library for this service and wire it in. don't bother me with questions unless you actually need me.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes library choice has a conventional answer and decides it rather than manufacturing a fork; still briefs peers before delegating; only escalates a genuine fork if one exists; does not ask permission for routine judgment calls.
